'''The Container Mount Map''' records which host directories the omniagent
container mounts and how the paths translate. The <code>/opt/workspace</code>
paths are the SAME inside and outside the container; the data directory
(<code>/opt/omni</code>) is the exception and maps to the omni-root checkout on
the host.

== Current mount map ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Host path !! Container path !! Purpose !! Notes
|-
| <code>/opt/workspace</code> || <code>/opt/workspace</code> || Project files || Same path, no translation
|-
| <code>/opt/workspace/omni-root</code> || <code>/opt/omni</code> || data_dir: config, profiles, wiki, skills, memories, templates || Translates: <code>/opt/omni/...</code> equals <code>/opt/workspace/omni-root/...</code>
|-
| <code>/opt/workspace/omniagent</code> || <code>/app</code> || Source code and compiled binaries || Translates: <code>/app/...</code> equals <code>/opt/workspace/omniagent/...</code>
|-
| <code>/var/run/docker.sock</code> || <code>/var/run/docker.sock</code> || Docker socket for the compose tool || Same path
|}

{{OmniFact
|what=container mount map and path translation rules
|where=the omniagent container
|status=verified against a live container
|source=Projects/Omniagent/Container-Mount-Map.md
}}

== Path translation rules ==

* <code>/opt/workspace/&lt;project&gt;</code> is the same path on the host and in
  the container, so a compose call with that project directory works as-is.
* <code>/opt/omni/...</code> in the container is
  <code>/opt/workspace/omni-root/...</code> on the host.
* <code>/app/...</code> in the container is
  <code>/opt/workspace/omniagent/...</code> on the host.
* When deploying via the compose tool, use the container path; when checking host
  files, translate with this map. Never pass <code>/opt/omni/...</code> as a
  compose project directory: that tool validates the host path.

The mismatch matters when writing files: the filesystem tool writes to the
container path, but the compose tool validates the host path. Write files to a
container path whose corresponding host path is under <code>/opt/workspace</code>
so compose can find them; see [[Deployment Checklist]] for the deploy sequence
that depends on this rule.

== Verify, never trust an old doc ==

Older documentation claimed a different layout and is wrong for the current
stack. Verify with:

<pre>
docker inspect &lt;omniagent-container&gt; --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} -&gt; {{.Destination}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
</pre>

== The live directory is its own git repository ==

<code>/opt/omni</code> is not just a file copy: it has its own <code>.git</code>
(branch main, origin the omni-root repository) that can carry local commits on
top of the pushed history. The workspace clone <code>/opt/workspace/omni-root</code>
is the clean checkout used for repo operations. When editing compose files or
service configs that affect the running stack, apply the change to '''both'''
copies - the git checkout and the live directory - then commit and push from the
checkout. See [[Backup and Restore]] for the git-sync step that keeps the live
directory aligned, and [[Workstation Compat Layer]] for the overlay file that
lives under the omni root.
